# NEAR investment thesis

## Thesis

**NEAR is an L1 with two fast-growing businesses behind its token. Revenue growth, combined with buybacks, burns and staking, makes it a solid long-term investment.** The two businesses are NEAR Intents, a cross-chain swap network, and NEAR AI, a private AI cloud. Intents brings the revenue: it now earns {c1_share3} of NEAR's protocol revenue, against {c1_share3_yago} a year earlier, and in {m} that revenue was {rev_x} its level a year before. NEAR AI is earlier and publishes no revenue yet, but its usage is growing fast: it served {ai_last} tokens on OpenRouter in the week to {ai_last_week}, {ai_x} its first full week. Burns and buybacks tie that revenue to the token: L1 fees are burned and Intents fees buy NEAR back, and together they offset {c6_ratio} of new NEAR in {c6_q}, against {c6_ratio_yago} a year earlier.{thesis_breakeven} Staking locks NEAR up: {thesis_staking} New supply is also falling: the cap on new issuance has been cut from {infl_from} to {infl_to} a year. We are long-term bullish. This report sets out the evidence for that view, the evidence against it, and what would change our mind.

## The problem NEAR solves

NEAR was built as an L1: a base-layer blockchain designed to be fast and cheap, and to scale by splitting its work across shards. Fees still average about {l1_fee} a transaction. It found early traction. Apps such as Sweat, HOT and KaiChing took off on it, and in {l1_tx_first_month} the chain carried {l1_tx_first} transactions a day.

But blockspace has become a commodity. Many chains now offer fast, cheap transactions, and cheap transactions earn little: in {m}, all of NEAR's L1 gas fees came to {l1_fees_usd}. The traffic did not last either. One app, KaiChing, sent {kc_share} of all L1 transactions in {kc_month}, and when it stopped the next month, L1 traffic fell with it. By {l1_tx_last_month} the L1 carried {l1_tx_last} transactions a day.

So NEAR has taken on two more problems: fragmented blockchains and centralised AI.

**Fragmented blockchains.** Crypto is spread across hundreds of blockchains, each with its own assets and apps. Moving money between them usually takes several steps, a bridge, and a fee at each one. **NEAR Intents** turns that into one step: a user says what they have and what they want, competing market makers fill the order, and NEAR settles the result. In {m}, Intents handled {int_vol} of swaps, {int_vol_x} its level a year earlier. On 1Click, the Intents channel with public swap-by-swap data, {int_users} users swapped through {int_apps} apps, starting from {int_chains} chains.

**Centralised AI.** A few companies run the most capable AI models, and they see everything people send them. **NEAR AI** runs open models inside secure hardware, so no one, not even NEAR AI, can read the prompts. Customers pay per use, or stake NEAR and receive AI credits. It is the newest business. On OpenRouter, a marketplace for AI models, it served {ai_last} tokens (units of text) in the week to {ai_last_week}, {ai_x} its first full week, and Brave's AI assistant has offered a model running on it since {brave_date}.

That makes NEAR three businesses on one token: the L1, NEAR Intents and NEAR AI. The rest of this paper breaks down each business, shows how it contributes to the NEAR token, and explains why we think that makes NEAR a good investment.

## NEAR's three layers

NEAR now works as three businesses, each built on the one below it. People, apps and AI agents come in at the top, and every layer connects to the NEAR token.

![NEAR's three layers, and the token they share](site/charts/three-layers.svg)

The layers are built to feed each other. AI agents that need to pay or trade across chains can do it through Intents, and every Intents swap settles on the L1.

## Why the NEAR token has value

The token gains when NEAR is taken out of circulation, or locked up, faster than new NEAR is issued. Four mechanisms do that, and each one started or changed in the last {mech_months} months.

- **Fees and burns.** Every L1 transaction pays a fee in NEAR. {gas_txt}
- **Buybacks.** NEAR keeps a share of the fees on Intents swaps. Since {bb_date}, that share buys NEAR on the market.
- **Staking.** NEAR is staked with validators to secure the chain: {stake_total} NEAR, {stake_pct} of all NEAR, on {stake_date}. Since {ai_open}, holders can also stake with NEAR AI and receive AI credits. Staked NEAR is locked, not removed, and can be withdrawn.
- **Less new supply.** On {infl_date}, NEAR cut its cap on new issuance from {infl_from} to {infl_to} a year. A second cut, HSP-029, passed on {hsp_passed} and would lower it to {hsp_target} by {hsp_end}.

![Follow the money: what each layer earned, how much NEAR is staked, and what reached the token](site/charts/money-flow.svg)

**How much it adds up to.** Burns and buybacks offset {c6_ratio} of the new NEAR issued in {c6_q}, against {c6_ratio_yago} a year earlier. Counting NEAR newly staked with NEAR AI, the figure reached {incl_ai}. Most new NEAR is still not offset, so the case depends on revenue continuing to grow.

![Share of new NEAR offset by burns and buybacks, monthly](site/charts/c6-ratio.svg)

**Where it could go.** {outlook} These are projections from a short history, not forecasts. The assumptions are in [METHODS.md](METHODS.md#scenarios).

![Where it could go: share of new NEAR offset by burns and buybacks, projected with HSP-029](site/charts/scenarios-hsp.svg)

## The last year, business by business

This section shows how each of NEAR's three businesses, and the token, changed over the twelve months to {m}. **NEAR Intents grew the most.** Swap volume rose {int_vol_x}, and its share of native cross-chain swap volume (against THORChain, Chainflip and Maya) rose from {c4_yago} to {c4_share} while total DEX volume {c4_dex_move}. **NEAR AI is new.** Its first full week on OpenRouter ended {ai_first_week}, and staking for AI credits opened on {ai_open}. In {m} it served {ai_month_tokens} tokens on OpenRouter and held {ai_staked} NEAR in stake. **The L1 moved the other way.** Its own traffic fell after its largest app left, and Intents now makes up {c2_share} of its transactions, against {c2_share_yago} a year earlier. **For the token,** burns and buybacks offset {offset_m} of new NEAR in {m}, against {offset_y} a year earlier.

{context_table}

> **Brave.** Brave's browser has over {brave_mau} monthly users. Since {brave_date}, its AI assistant Leo offers {brave_model} running on NEAR AI Cloud, so Leo users who pick that model get private AI they can verify. {customers}

**Where NEAR stands today.** It is worth being direct about this. Intents is a working, growing business, and it already pays for buybacks. NEAR AI is early: it publishes no revenue, and we estimate its OpenRouter sales at about {ai_annual} a year. The token is earliest of all, because the mechanisms that send value to it have only just been switched on. But revenue is growing fast, and burns, buybacks and staking connect that growth to the token, which is why our view is long-term bullish.
